title: Grondpannenkoek
excerpt: Grondpannenkoek (ground pancake), also called straatpannenkoek, is Dutch slang for vomit on the floor. The same as a grondpizza.
example: After the third shot the night sadly ended in a big grondpannenkoek.
text: Dutch students have a surprising number of food words for throwing up. Grondpannenkoek, straatpannenkoek and grondpizza all mean the same unlucky thing. Appetising, right?

title: Grondpizza
excerpt: A grondpizza (ground pizza) is Dutch slang for vomit on the floor, usually in a roughly round shape.
example: Leaving the club, they had to watch out for a stray grondpizza.
text: You see them outside clubs at the end of a night. The term is also used when it lands in a urinal instead of on the floor. Eating well before you go out, or bodem leggen, helps you avoid making one.

title: Group project
excerpt: A group project is an assignment you do together with other students.
example: "Four people in my group project and I'm the only one doing anything."
text: A group project is supposed to teach you how to work together. It is also famous for unfair task splits, impossible planning and chaotic group chats. There is always someone who only shows up the night before the deadline.

title: GRWM
excerpt: GRWM stands for Get Ready With Me. A video where someone gets ready for a night out or an event.
example: "GRWM for the first gala of the year. Spoiler: I'm late again."
text: In a GRWM video you film yourself getting dressed or doing your make-up. Usually you talk to the camera about your day or a story at the same time. It is a mix of fashion, beauty and storytime.

title: Guac
excerpt: Guac is short for guacamole, the Mexican avocado dip.
example: At the nacho night the guac obviously couldn't be missing.
text: The dip is avocado, chilli, salt and lime juice. You find it with crisps at almost every student borrel. And yes, it always costs extra.

title: Guest list
excerpt: A guest list is a list of people who get into a party or club.
example: "Don't worry about the queue. I put us on the guest list."
text: Being on the guest list usually means you are sure to get in. Sometimes you get a discount, skip the queue or don't pay a cover charge. The bouncer checks your name at the door.

title: Guilty pleasure
excerpt: A guilty pleasure is something you secretly enjoy, even though you know it isn't really cool or good.
example: "My guilty pleasure? Watching Temptation Island every Sunday with a bag of crisps."
text: A guilty pleasure can be a cheesy song, a terrible reality show or fast food at three in the morning. You are a bit ashamed of it, but you wouldn't want to miss it. Usually you admit it lowkey.

title: Haasje
excerpt: Haasje (little hare) is the male version of hertje, used in Dutch corps circles for an attractive guy.
example: At the sociëteit she laughingly pointed him out as the cutest haasje of the night.
text: The word is mostly used within traditional corps student associations. Male members there call women hertjes. Haasje is the answer from the other side. Cheeky, old-fashioned and very corps.

title: Hair of the dog
excerpt: Hair of the dog is the idea that you fight a hangover by drinking alcohol again the next morning.
example: "I feel terrible." "Have a beer with breakfast. Hair of the dog."
text: The Dutch know this as the herstelbiertje, the recovery beer. It might feel better for a moment, but it only delays your recovery. Water, food and sleep are what really help. The saying comes from an old idea that you heal a dog bite with hair from the same dog.

title: Halve leo
excerpt: A halve leo is a half-litre can of beer.
example: For the road he preferred a halve leo over a normal can.
text: It is bigger than a standard can, so you need fewer of them to last the whole party. A classic for the bike ride to a party. Pair it with a bvo and you are set.

title: Hangover
excerpt: A hangover is the awful feeling the day after drinking too much.
example: "After the gala I had the worst hangover of my life. I spent all of Sunday on the couch."
text: With a hangover you often have a headache, thirst, nausea and zero focus. The Dutch call it a kater, and the lazy, useless version is called brak. Time, water and rest help most. Drinking again the next day is called hair of the dog.

title: Happy hour
excerpt: Happy hour is a time slot when a bar or restaurant sells drinks at a discount.
example: "Happy hour is between five and seven. Two cocktails for the price of one."
text: Despite the name, happy hour often lasts longer than an hour. Perfect for a broke student. Lots of students plan their borrel around the happy hour of their favourite bar.

title: Hard launch
excerpt: A hard launch is announcing something openly and officially, like showing your new partner on social media.
example: "She posted a photo of both their faces, with his name tagged. That's a hard launch."
text: A hard launch is the opposite of a soft launch. In dating you clearly show your partner or say their name. No more guessing. It often comes after a few weeks of soft launching.

title: Hater
excerpt: A hater is someone who keeps criticising or putting someone else down.
example: "Everyone liked his new haircut except his housemate. Just a hater."
text: Haters gonna hate, as they say. The word is often used lightly. Sometimes to brush off criticism that is actually fair. Anyone who gets successful online automatically collects a few haters.

title: Heavyweight
excerpt: In drinking slang, a heavyweight is someone who can drink a lot before they seem drunk.
example: "After eight beers he was still standing straight. A real heavyweight."
text: The opposite is a lightweight. A high tolerance doesn't mean drinking a lot is safe. Someone can seem sober and still have a high blood alcohol level. Dutch students would say this person can bakken vouwen all night.

title: Her
excerpt: Her is Dutch student slang for a resit. Short for "hertentamen".
example: After a fail she had to prepare for her her in January.
text: A her gives you a second chance at an exam you didn't pass the first time. Usually a few weeks after the original exam. Confusing for English speakers, because "her her" is a real sentence in Dutch student life.

title: Herstelbiertje
excerpt: A herstelbiertje (recovery beer) is a beer you drink to get rid of a hangover.
example: The next morning he opened a herstelbiertje straight away, hoping to feel a bit better.
text: Does it really help? Debatable. But among students who stayed out all night it is a fixed ritual. In English this is called hair of the dog. Some prefer a reparadler, the lighter version with lemonade.

title: Hertje
excerpt: Hertje (little deer) is Dutch student slang for an attractive woman, mostly used in corps circles.
example: During the gala the guys were giggling about "hunting hertjes".
text: Male members of traditional corps associations use it for women. The male version is haasje. It is old-fashioned and a bit cheesy. You will mostly hear it at the sociëteit.

title: HG
excerpt: HG is short for "huisgenoot", the Dutch word for housemate.
example: "Is there a HG home who wants to eat with us?" my friend asked.
text: Dutch students live with a lot of HG's. The newest one is the huisjongste, or HJ, and gets the most chores. In English you would say flatmate.

title: Highkey
excerpt: Highkey means very much, or openly and without shame. The opposite of lowkey.
example: "I'm highkey excited for the gala on Saturday."
text: With highkey you make clear you really mean something and everyone can know it. Where lowkey tones things down, highkey makes them bigger.

title: Hila
excerpt: Hila is Dutch student slang for hilarious.
example: "That video from yesterday was so hila," she said, laughing out loud.
text: You mostly see it in texts and stories about situations that are just too absurd to keep a straight face. Same meaning as in English, half the letters.

title: HJ
excerpt: HJ has two meanings among Dutch students: huisjongste (the newest housemate) or the beer brand Hertog Jan.
example: "Are you the HJ here? Then you must be doing the dishes."
text: In a student house HJ means huisjongste, the housemate who moved in last. At the bar the same letters mean Hertog Jan, a popular Dutch beer. Usually it is clear which one people mean. Usually.

title: Honk
excerpt: Honk (base) is the Dutch version of the bases system: how far you got with someone physically.
example: "So how far did you get? Second honk already?" her housemate asked.
text: It works just like the American bases. First honk is kissing, or huig hockeyen as Dutch students say. Every next honk is a step further, all the way up to the fourth. The word comes from baseball, which the Dutch call honkbal.

title: Hookup
excerpt: A hookup is a short, casual romantic or sexual moment without a relationship or commitment.
example: "Was that something serious with him?" "Nah, just a hookup after the party."
text: A hookup can be kissing, but also sex. It often stays a one-time thing. Apps like Tinder are often used to find one. The Dutch word scharrel is similar, but a scharrel usually lasts a bit longer.

title: Hospi
excerpt: Hospi is short for hospiteren: the viewing evening where a Dutch student house picks a new housemate.
example: She went to five hospi's that week, looking for a nice room.
text: Students use the short version just as often as the full word. Going to a lot of hospi's is a rite of passage when you are looking for a room in a Dutch city. It is basically a group vibe check.

title: Hospiteren
excerpt: Hospiteren is the Dutch way of finding a housemate: the current housemates invite candidates and pick who gets the room.
example: To go hospiteren she put on her best outfit and practised a few jokes.
text: When a room frees up in a Dutch student house, the housemates invite people over for a chat and a drink. Then they decide who fits best. It is mostly about personality, not your CV. For internationals it is good to know that some houses say "Dutch only" in their ads. Plenty of others are happy to have you.

title: Hot take
excerpt: A hot take is a strong or controversial opinion, often meant to start a discussion.
example: "Hot take: frikandellen are better than kroketten." Half the table disagreed.
text: Online you say hot take for an opinion you expect others to disagree with. Sometimes it is exaggerated on purpose as a joke. It is close to an unpopular opinion.

title: Houdini
excerpt: A houdini is Dutch student slang for sneaking out of a night out without saying goodbye.
example: Halfway through the night he was suddenly gone without a trace. Another houdini.
text: Named after the famous escape artist. In English this is called an Irish goodbye or a French exit. Dutch students also call it taking the rattentaxi.

title: House party
excerpt: A house party is a party at someone's home instead of at a bar or club.
example: "House party at ours on Saturday. Bring your own drinks and leave the neighbours alone."
text: A house party can be small, with a few friends in the living room. Or a whole student house packed with people. It is often BYOB. A fixed part of student life everywhere.

title: Huig hockeyen
excerpt: Huig hockeyen (uvula hockey) is Dutch student slang for French kissing.
example: Suddenly they were loudly huig hockeyen on the dance floor.
text: The huig is your uvula, that little thing at the back of your throat. So you can picture the rest. It is the first step on the honk scale, the Dutch version of the bases.

title: Huisjongste
excerpt: The huisjongste (HJ) is the housemate who moved into the student house most recently.
example: As huisjongste she always had to empty the dishwasher for the first few months.
text: The huisjongste often gets the most chores. Taking out the bins, cleaning up after a party, buying the house beer. Until a new HG moves in and the role moves on. Some houses go easy on it. Others take it very seriously.

title: Huispanda
excerpt: The huispanda (house panda) is the housemate who hasn't had sex for the longest time.
example: As a joke they gave this year's huispanda a real bamboo plant to look after.
text: Pandas are famous for rarely mating, hence the name. In some student houses the title comes with a plant as a symbolic gift. The score is kept in pandapunten. All in good fun. Mostly.

title: Huisparasiet
excerpt: A huisparasiet (house parasite) is someone who hangs out at a student house all the time, without living there.
example: Officially he didn't live there, but as huisparasiet he was around more than most housemates.
text: Usually it is the partner or best friend of a housemate. They eat the food, sit in the GR and know where the spare key is. After a while they belong to the house just as much as the people paying rent.

title: Hustle culture
excerpt: Hustle culture is the idea that you should always be working and achieving, even if it costs you your rest.
example: "Up at five, gym, study, work and then a side hustle too. That hustle culture is not normal."
text: On social media hustle culture is often glorified. Long days, always productive and measuring your worth by your success. The word is usually used critically. Live like that too long and you risk a burnout.

title: HV
excerpt: HV stands for "huisvergadering", the house meeting where housemates make decisions about the student house.
example: At the HV they finally decided who was in charge of the house beer.
text: During a HV housemates talk about things like hospiteren, repairs, the cleaning rota and the shared living room. Sometimes it is five minutes. Sometimes it takes all night and a crate of beer.

title: Ibu
excerpt: Ibu is Dutch student slang for ibuprofen, often needed after a big night out.
example: Before going to bed, she took an ibu just in case.
text: Lots of students grab one the day after going out, ideally with a big glass of water. The other classic is para, short for paracetamol. Neither one fixes a brak Sunday completely though.

title: Icing
excerpt: Icing is a drinking game where you hide a Smirnoff Ice for someone. Whoever finds it has to chug it.
example: Under the couch he suddenly found a bottle of Smirnoff Ice. He got iced.
text: Find a hidden bottle and you have to drink it in one go, often on one knee. Already busy with another game? Then you have to finish the bottle before you can join again. The Dutch call it icen.

title: Ick
excerpt: An ick is a small habit or trait that suddenly turns you off someone completely.
example: "He ran after his ping pong ball during beer pong. Instant ick."
text: Icks are often irrational and very personal. Think of how someone eats, walks or writes a text. It is a sudden turn-off, not a real problem. Real problems are a dealbreaker or a red flag.

title: IDC
excerpt: IDC stands for I don't care.
example: "Pizza or sushi tonight?" "IDC, as long as there's food."
text: IDC can sound blunt, so context matters. Among friends it often just means you don't mind. In an argument it sounds a lot colder.

title: IDK
excerpt: IDK stands for I don't know.
example: "What time does the party start anyway?" "IDK, ask in the group chat."
text: IDK is one of the most used abbreviations in texts. Depending on the tone it sounds casual, unsure or uninterested. Often written in lowercase as idk.

title: IJskast
excerpt: IJskast (ice cupboard) is an old-fashioned Dutch word for the fridge that students love to use.
example: "Is the beer in the ijskast yet?" she shouted from the hallway.
text: Most Dutch people say koelkast. Students say ijskast, mostly when it is about the drinks for tonight. In a student house the ijskast is a battlefield of labelled food and missing eggs.

title: I'm weak
excerpt: You say I'm weak when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
example: She sent a photo of her housemate who fell asleep with his head in the pan. "I'm weak."
text: I'm weak is close to I'm dead. It means you can't take it anymore from laughing. You see it in texts, comments and under memes.

title: IMO
excerpt: IMO stands for in my opinion.
example: "IMO the second party was way better than the first."
text: With IMO you show something is your own opinion, not a fact. There is also IMHO: in my humble opinion. That adds a bit of modesty. Or a lot of irony.

title: Imposter syndrome
excerpt: Imposter syndrome is the feeling that you are not as good as people think, and that you could be found out any moment.
example: "Everyone in my master seems so smart. I feel like I got in by accident." Classic imposter syndrome.
text: Imposter syndrome is really common among students and starters. Even with good results it feels like you just got lucky. It is a pattern of self-doubt. Talking about it with others often helps already.

title: In my ___ era
excerpt: In my ___ era means you are in a certain phase. You fill in the blank yourself.
example: "I go to bed at ten every day. I'm in my healthy era."
text: Almost anything fits in the blank. Your villain era, your single era or your study era. It is a fun way to joke about changing priorities. You see it a lot in captions and TikToks.

title: Inauguratie
excerpt: An inauguratie is the official ceremony where someone becomes a full member of a Dutch student association.
example: During the inauguratie she was officially welcomed as a full member.
text: The ceremony often marks the end of the introduction period. New members are voted in, which is called instemmen, and then celebrated. Expect speeches, suits and a long night.

title: Indikken
excerpt: Indikken (to thicken) is what Dutch students shout to get a group to stand or sit closer together.
example: "Can you guys indikken?" the barco shouted when it got too crowded at the tap.
text: You mostly hear it when a sociëteit or student house is packed and everyone has to squeeze in. Think of it as "budge up", but louder. Usually followed by groans and laughter.

title: Indrinken
excerpt: Indrinken means drinking at home before going out, because drinks at the bar are expensive.
example: Before going out they agreed to indrinken at her place first.
text: Drinks from the supermarket are way cheaper than at a bar or club. So everyone has a few beers at home first. Sometimes with a bvo for on the way. In English this is called pre-drinks, pre-gaming or pres.

title: Influ
excerpt: Influ is Dutch slang for an influencer, someone with lots of followers online.
example: "Don't be such an influ," she joked when he took a photo for the fifth time.
text: Students also use it in a teasing way for someone who takes way too many photos of themselves. Ordering food and taking ten pictures before eating? Very influ.

title: Inkakken
excerpt: Inkakken is the feeling of getting tired and sluggish during a night out.
example: Around midnight he was already starting to inkakken on the couch.
text: It happens when you are tired or haven't had a drink in a while. The night slips away from you. The student advice is simple: "bijpakken", grab another drink. Or just go home and admit you are cooked.
